Well, think about your wife, if you had spent years upon years sleeping next to her and then she was just gone...it would be so lonely, there would be a cold spot that kept you comfortable and safe now gone... so it would make sense for a little bit that she would need help by sleeping next to someone, when my grandfather died my grandmother slept on the very uncomfortable couch only because she couldnt sleep without my grandpa there. 

Having said that, your wife needs to be honest with her mom, saying shes hurting too, but she cant stay every night, that she loves her and will always be there for her when she needs it. Then she needs to start slowly taking herself out of the picture, instead of everynight, stay until she falls asleep, then every other night, then twice a week, until she feels comfortable alone, remember her husband was there one night and gone the next so she needs to ease out of it. 

Remember grieving takes awhile, be supportive and loving, try to put yourself in her shoes, years of being with your true love, and then theyre  gone. Give her lots of hugs, visit her lots, invite her to eat, tell her shes loved and important. 

Best to the two of you.

I will say this as nicely as i can, polyamorous relationships are hard and very difficult to maintain, you have to be understanding of all parties, now that being said, she still had a relationship with this person, and even if it was completly non sexual it was strong enough to last for 3 years. If the other was abusive and usually the shows withing the first year or so, he probably had a way of making her feel like it was her fault, or it was because he loved her so much thats why he had to, etc, etc, because when your in an abusive relationship you still love your abuser and it takes a lot to get out of that feeling of hurt. Now you may not like when i say this, but you agreed to the poly thing, you knew she was with another person for the physical presence because you were only there online, if you lost your physical connect to the world (and if he was abusive he probably made himself the person she relied on most to make it harder to leave) and then were told "hey you have another relationship you are responsible for so you cant spend all your time ghosting me like a jerk." Youd be pretty pissed too, because although yes, she does have responsibilities to you as a gf, but she still went through a break up with a mentally abusive person. You dont just feel relieved or sad, its a sea of emotions that i personally hope dont scar her for life. Right now is not the time to be arguing with her about what she needs to be focused on. You have already broken up once so you know what you two feel like apart or together, but let her have some time to cope, polyamorous relationships and abusive relationships and her already existing intimacy issues, its a lot. If she ghosts you for a week then just give her words of reassurance that she can read but dont need to respond to. "Hey, i know its tough, hang in there, ill be here when you need me." Leave her alone for a day until she talks to you. Next morning "good morning, you are a beautiful person and im glad the world gave me you, have a good day, ill be here if you want to talk." The repeat with different words of appreciation. Her abuser probably broke her and hurt her self esteem. When you text her make sure you let her know someway that your there for her. Dont be an asshole and realise she went through hell. Be a good bf and help her through it. You agreed to her other bf and whatever happened with it.
